HISTORICAL FCF on this series is levered free cash flow after stock-based compensation (house default: operating cash flow + capital expenditure − SBC; unadjusted only where SBC was not disclosed), stated AFTER interest. It is not the before-SBC vendor figure behind the FCF CAGR. The two segments share the SBC treatment but differ on leverage: for a leveraged issuer the level steps at the history→forecast seam by roughly after-tax interest, and that step is a change of basis, not a forecast of improvement.

Scenario paths can cross: the higher-growth shock reinvests more up front, so its near-term FCF may sit below the lower-growth shock. The bull-to-bear spread is the scenario range; bull/bear labels do not imply an ordering of each operating metric.

Operating EPS = (forward operating EBIT − interest expense 3.8B a year at the latest quarter's run-rate (the quarter ending 2026-03-28's interest 0.95B × 4), held flat) × (1 − that year's DCF tax rate) ÷ diluted shares with applied change 0%/yr (year-one net income / EBIT 0.83). Interest income, investment gains and other non-operating items are excluded, so this is operating EPS, not a forecast of GAAP diluted EPS.

The base holds the diluted share count flat: a repurchase authorization is discretionary capacity, not a committed schedule, and future repurchases depend on cash and price. Positive dilution is retained only when the observed share-count trend is positive. No remaining repurchase authorization was read from the filings. The historical-share-trend alternative is hypothetical and does not deduct repurchase cash from equity value; flat-share EPS isolates operating performance.

Operating EPS = (forward operating EBIT − interest expense 3.8B a year at the latest quarter's run-rate (the quarter ending 2026-03-28's interest 0.95B × 4), held flat) × (1 − that year's DCF tax rate) ÷ diluted shares with applied change 0%/yr (year-one net income / EBIT 0.83). Interest income, investment gains and other non-operating items are excluded, so this is operating EPS, not a forecast of GAAP diluted EPS.

The base holds the diluted share count flat: a repurchase authorization is discretionary capacity, not a committed schedule, and future repurchases depend on cash and price. Positive dilution is retained only when the observed share-count trend is positive. No remaining repurchase authorization was read from the filings. The historical-share-trend alternative is hypothetical and does not deduct repurchase cash from equity value; flat-share EPS isolates operating performance.
